instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to perform a tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Part: Instantiate a 3D Deformable Shell part. Sketch a rectangle on the XY plane with dimensions 120 mm in the X direction and 240 mm in the Y direction. Cut a circular hole at the center point (60, 120) mm with a diameter of 12 mm. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with thickness 1 mm and 5 through-thickness integration points. Assign the section to the entire plate geometry. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shell plate. Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-HoleTension, placing it after the Initial step. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply shell edge loads of 8 N/mm to the two vertical outer edges. On the left edge at X = 0, apply the load in the global negative X direction. On the right edge at X = 120, apply the load in the global positive X direction. To prevent rigid-body motion without over-constraining the tensile deformation: - At the bottom-left corner (0, 0), constrain U1 = U2 = U3 = 0. - At the bottom-right corner (120, 0), constrain U2 = U3 = 0. - At the top-left corner (0, 240), constrain U3 = 0. Mesh: Seed the circular hole edge with an approximate element size of 2.4 mm. Apply a global seed size of 10 mm to the plate. Assign element type appropriate shell element formulation and generate the mesh. Job: Create a job named Job-FlangeHole, submit it, and wait for successful completion. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` with numeric fields for the requested metrics.
